subject: Issues with MESS plotting through ggplot2

messages.author: cbebdaa89cf1945e
messages.subject: Issues with MESS plotting through ggplot2
parts:
Hi Wallace Team!

I'm running the model of a species that has a cis-andean distribution. My goal is to project this model in trans-andean areas. Therefore, I run MESS to find out the areas that are climatically different from the areas associated with occs. My goal is to get the MESS prediction map to use in a manuscript. However,  Wallace generates the MESS map through the leaflet library, which doesn't allow to download of the plot in PDF. To solve this problem, I have generated a code using ggplot2. However, I have encountered some issues:

1) Even though I use the same object to generate the map, the plot created with ggplot2 (MESS_ggplot2.jpg) is not the same as the generated with leaflet (MESS_leaflet.jpg). The prediction intensities are not the same, so it is unreliable.
2) When I add the MESS prediction with geom_raster, I must use "fill = as.factor (mess)", because if I don't get the following error: Continuous value supplied to discrete scale. Due to the mess variable is being read as a factor, the plot legend is too long (Legend_labels.jpg).

Also, I have reviewed the ENMeval vignette that also talks about MESS, but the ENMeval way doesn't use the background as it does the Wallace workflow. I'm only trying to find the simplest way to plot the MESS map using ggplot2 so that it is the same map generated with the leaflet library. Any help or recommendation? I attach the code (MESS_Wallace.Rmd) that I'm using to generate the MESS plot.

Best, and I wish you a merry Christmas.
Jhan.

messages.author: 881c0dd9c7b0d196
messages.subject: Re: Issues with MESS plotting through ggplot2
parts:
Hi Jhan! 
Is your desired end result to get the MESS map as a pdf? If that's the case, I'd download it as a PNG (which is an available option through the Wallace GUI) and then export that to a pdf. 
If there is another reason you are using ggplot2, I can put you in touch with someone from the team who knows a bit more about leaflet and ggplot when they are back from winter break.
Happy holidays.

-Bethany
